items.title: Trump says will declare Hormuz US territory 'pretty soon'; US eyes indefinite Iran naval blockade
items.content: US-Israel war on Iran live updates: Trump says will declare Strait of Hormuz US territory 'pretty soon', US eyes indefinite Iran naval blockade. Conflict in the strait continues to dominate energy markets.

items.title: Trump insists US controls Hormuz, Iran says it could 'prolong' war with US
items.content: President Trump insisted the US still has control over the Strait of Hormuz, threatening Iran would 'get blown away' if it tried to 'do something'. The waterway has again become center-stage in the conflict.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz: conflict resumed July 2026 as Iran attacks commercial shipping
items.content: US and Iran agreed a ceasefire in April 2026 and signed a June 2026 MOU, but conflict resumed in July 2026 as Iranian forces launched attacks on commercial shipping deemed noncompliant with Iranian demands. Oil, gas and commodity supply via the strait remain at risk.

items.title: 2026 Iran war: Iran seeks hegemonic control of Strait of Hormuz despite June MoU
items.content: Despite the June 2026 MoU seeking to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Iran war, Iran sought to assert hegemonic control over the strait and collect fees on ships passing through.

items.title: S&P 500 notches record close of 7,798.99, surpassing 7,800 for first time
items.content: S&P 500 rose to a fresh closing record of 7,798.99, breaking above 7,800 for the first time ever; Dow also posted record closes. Tech jumped 4%.

items.title: S&P 500 slides on Friday but notches third consecutive weekly advance
items.content: Broad market index closed down 0.2% to 7,785.76 on Friday, Nasdaq Composite shed 0.3% to 26,729.16, yet the benchmark still posted its third consecutive weekly gain after a record-setting week.

items.title: Russell 2000 notches fresh record to cap off week; S&P clears 7,800
items.content: Stock futures mixed after S&P 500 closed at record high clearing 7,800 for the first time; Russell 2000 hit a fresh record to cap off the week, small caps participating in the rally.

items.title: Hang Seng slips 0.8% to 25,440 as fading US-Iran deal hopes weigh
items.content: Hang Seng Index slipped 0.8% to close at 25,440 on Wednesday, as fading hopes for a US-Iran deal and caution ahead of the latest US inflation data weighed on investor sentiment. Investors also monitored upcoming corporate earnings and China tech developments.

items.title: China stocks end mixed; SMIC Q2 profit more than triples on AI chip demand
items.content: Shanghai Composite flat at 3,927.2, Shenzhen Component +0.45% to 14,354.3. Semiconductor stocks gained after SMIC reported more than threefold increase in second-quarter profit on strong AI-related chip demand, offsetting US tariff concerns.

items.title: Geopolitical risk is the new normal: Hormuz conflict hits Asian supply chains
items.content: Asia faces shortages in fertilizer (food supply), chemicals (tech hardware) and plastics (autos, pharma), sparking double-digit price increases in weeks. Even a rapid reopening of the Strait could leave an 'air pocket' as supply chains normalize slowly.

items.title: Geopolitical Risk Dashboard: Gulf conflict's impact on global energy markets still unfolding
items.content: BlackRock's August 2026 geopolitical risk dashboard highlights the Gulf conflict's still-unfolding implications for global energy markets, Western interests and geopolitical relationships across the Gulf and beyond.

items.title: Stock market turmoil sheds stark light on opaque AI economy
items.content: China reportedly developed its own deep-ultraviolet lithography tools, breaking ASML's monopoly in a chip supply chain essential step. AI-linked shares, particularly chipmakers, dropped around the world; Kospi fell 11.5% in a day on SK Hynix and Samsung losses. Context for continued semiconductor volatility.
